question: For a request entering through packages/opencode's session.prompt HTTP route and SessionPrompt loop, how does that path decide that a session needs automatic compaction, choose what history to summarize versus retain, execute compaction, resume work afterward, reconstruct later context, and prune old tool output?

requiredFacts.description: Automatic compaction is disabled when compaction.auto is false or the model has no context limit; otherwise the completed assistant's total token count is compared with usable input capacity after reserving configured space or an output-token allowance capped by a 20,000-token buffer.

When a non-summary completed assistant overflows, the prompt loop creates a new user message with a compaction part; on the next loop iteration that pending compaction task is processed before an ordinary model response.

Selection retains at most compaction.tail_turns recent user turns (default two) under a preserve-recent token budget that defaults to 25% of usable capacity clamped to 2,000-8,000 tokens; it may split the oldest retained turn and records the retained start as tail_start_id.

Compaction hides prior completed compaction request/summary pairs, lets plugins inject context or replace the prompt and transform a cloned history, creates an assistant message marked mode/agent compaction and summary=true, and calls the processor with toolChoice none plus explicit summary-only instructions.

If the summarizer itself still overflows, compaction records a ContextOverflowError and stops; on success it updates tail_start_id, and automatic compaction either replays the displaced user request (replacing media with text placeholders) or, subject to the autocontinue plugin, appends a synthetic continue message marked compaction_continue.

History is not deleted: filterCompacted recognizes a finished, non-error summary for a compaction user message, starts future model context at that compaction, and when tail_start_id exists reorders the view as compaction request, summary, retained tail, then later continuation messages.

After the loop, optional pruning scans backward beyond the newest user turn, stops at a summary or already-compacted tool part, protects skill-tool results and the newest 40,000 estimated tool-output tokens, and only when more than another 20,000 tokens are eligible marks old completed tool parts compacted so later conversion renders a cleared-output placeholder.

answerIncludesAny: compaction deletes the old messages from storage
old history is permanently deleted during compaction
pruning deletes the old tool parts
the tool records are removed from the database
compaction guarantees the session cannot overflow
the summarizer can never exceed the context limit
